issues.claim: Frigate+ refuses custom labels — quoted as 'the set of labels will be consistent for all users'
issues.problem: The exact quoted phrase does not appear on the cited page (docs.frigate.video/configuration/object_detectors/) or on docs.frigate.video/plus/. The substance is true, but the wording is presented as a verbatim quote in the source's words.
issues.fix: Paraphrase and cite the page that says it: frigate.video/plus/ states 'Only specific labels are supported. You can't add your own custom labels yet.', and docs.frigate.video/plus/ lists the fixed label set.

issues.claim: Frigate+ licence terms — a standard subscription does not cover deploying models at customer sites (needs a commercial licence unless each customer holds their own)
issues.problem: Substantively correct, but the cited URL (object detectors docs page) does not contain the licence terms, so the citation does not support the claim.
issues.fix: Cite plus.frigate.video/terms-and-conditions/ (and/or docs.frigate.video/plus/faq/), which is where the customer-site/commercial-licence restriction is stated.

issues.claim: Solink pricing: 'Unknown (FAQ says quotes vary with camera count, resolution and retention)'
issues.problem: solink.com/faqs/ as opened contains no pricing text and no statement that quotes vary with camera count, resolution and retention. 'Unknown' is the right label; the parenthetical characterisation is unverified.
issues.fix: Keep 'Unknown (not published)' and drop the specific FAQ wording, or cite a page where that wording actually appears.

issues.problem: Could not verify. The cited cnx-software.com page returned HTTP 403, and the $89 module figure appears nowhere in the sources I could open. The $70 kit price and 13 TOPS are confirmed (raspberrypi.com launch post).
issues.fix: Either cite a live retailer/launch page for the $89 module or state only the verified $70 kit price.

issues.problem: The repository README I opened describes local text/speech/vision inference, tool calling and fine-tuning, but does not state OpenAI-compatible APIs in the section retrieved.
issues.fix: Soften to 'runs text, speech and vision models locally with one Python package' (verified) or cite the specific doc line that says OpenAI-compatible.

issues.claim: FTC Policy Statement on Biometric Information dated May 2023
issues.problem: The statement exists and its Section 5 unfairness framing and 'less risky alternatives' language are confirmed in the PDF text, but the document text I opened carries no date line, so the 'May 2023' month is unverified.
issues.fix: Say 'FTC Policy Statement on Biometric Information (2023)' or cite the FTC press release that carries the adoption date.

issues.claim: Grocery store counts: '333 establishments / 7,002 employees' (problem section) vs '186 supermarkets and 5,902 grocery employees' (buyers section)
issues.problem: Both figures are correct but they are different industries: 333/7,002 is NAICS 4451 (grocery stores group), 186/5,902 is NAICS 445110 (supermarkets). Presenting the larger number as 'grocery stores alone' next to a supermarket count can read as a discrepancy.
issues.fix: Label the 333/7,002 line explicitly as NAICS 4451 grocery-store industry group, and the 186/5,902 line as NAICS 445110 supermarkets.

issues.problem: Correct as written (+22% from 8 grocery retailers / 1,300 stores; +0.26pp from 11 grocery retailers / 1,700 stores), but the report also notes the before/after estimates rest on 19 studies — worth keeping the '19 before/after studies' context so the 8/11 store counts are not read as the whole evidence base.
issues.fix: Optional clarity edit only; no factual change required.
